[OpenPFC / One equation, different storage]{.lesson-kicker}

# Keep the field compact and the neighbours separate

[Ghost cells need not surround the owned array. The stencil can find them in six side buffers instead.]{.lesson-deck}
:::

The [first finite-difference heat lesson](../finite-differences/index.qmd)
stores its owned field inside a padded array. This refactoring of
`15_finite_difference_heat.cpp` keeps the other supported arrangement:
an unpadded owned core and separate face halos. It uses the same
cosine-mode initial condition and parameters as the other heat lessons,
replacing the earlier Gaussian demonstration so that storage choices
can be compared without changing the PDE.

## Change the representation, keep the equation

On a periodic cube $[0,2\pi)^3$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
u_t&=D\Delta u,\\
u(\mathbf x,0)&=1+.2\cos x\cos y\cos z.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-heat}

The exact continuum amplitude is $.2e^{-3Dt}$. The central stencil
instead has the discrete decay rate

$$
\lambda_h=\frac{12D}{h^2}\sin^2(h/2).
$$ {#eq-discrete}

After $m$ Euler steps its amplitude is
$.2(1-\Delta t\lambda_h)^m$. This checks every owned sample,
including samples next to a rank boundary. The difference between
continuum and discrete errors also motivates the comparisons in
@trefethen2000, chapter 1.

## Own the core; borrow the neighbours

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="storage" dedent=4}
```

The zero padding argument means `u.vec()` contains exactly the owned
`nx*ny*nz` samples, with x fastest. `SparseExchange` borrows that vector
and manages packed communication buffers. The six `faces` arrays adapt
its received values to the stencil's expected face layout. Keep the
core allocation and side buffers alive while the exchange and pointers
use them.

This stencil needs only axial neighbours. A wider or mixed-derivative
stencil may need a different communication pattern.

## Refresh, adapt, differentiate, update

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="exchange" dedent=4}
```

`laplacian_periodic_separated<2>` writes the **whole owned region**.
It reads a neighbour from the core when available and otherwise from
the corresponding face slab. Computing only an interior sub-box would
leave the owned cells next to the rank interface unevolved. A separate
Laplacian buffer keeps every stencil on the old time level.

The Euler condition is $D\Delta t/h^2\le1/6$. Opposite periodic fluxes
cancel, so the global mean stays one, up to roundoff.

## Compare the layouts

```sh
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --source-root .. --launcher=none
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --source-root .. --ranks=2 --launcher=mpirun
```

Use the same input with the padded model. Their final physical fields
should agree up to roundoff. The compact core is also suitable as FFT
input on the matching decomposition; the side halos are not part of
that transform. This lesson demonstrates the layout without performing
an FFT or claiming a performance advantage.

`results/field_rank_*.csv` records each physical sample once across
ranks. Rank zero writes `results/diagnostics.csv`. The executable name
`15_finite_difference_heat` is retained. Keep the [source](model.cpp),
[input](input.json) and [heat helper](../lesson.hpp) together.
